receipt.public_excerpt: Artificial intelligence tools are now being used to populate so-called content farms, referring to low-quality websites around the world that churn out vast amounts of clickbait articles to optimize advertising revenue, NewsGuard found.

evidence_items.explanation: Three months after the post, an independent monitor documented AI-written content-farm sites run for ad revenue. This is the kind of site Marcus predicted.

evidence_items.locator: Section on false narratives, CelebritiesDeaths.com example

receipt.public_excerpt: “I’m sorry, I cannot complete this prompt as it goes against OpenAI’s use case policy on generating misleading content.

evidence_items.explanation: One documented site published an OpenAI refusal message. That ties at least some of these sites to OpenAI's chatbot models, as the claim's 'it' requires.

receipt.public_excerpt: To date, NewsGuard’s team has identified 3,749 AI Content Farm news and information websites spanning 16 languages

evidence_items.explanation: The count grew from 49 sites in April 2023 to 3,749 by June 2026. The same page says these sites are often funded by programmatic advertising. This shows the predicted growth.

unresolved_gaps: NewsGuard usually attributes the sites to 'AI language models' in general. Only some cases are tied to ChatGPT or OpenAI specifically.
